lessons.title: ট (ṭô) — the fourth corner
lessons.gloss: the fourth corner — the retroflex stop with the voice switched off, and the letter that has been blocking a whole grammar

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write ত, then দ, then ড. Say for each one where the tongue goes and whether the voice is on.

segments.instruction: two chapters back, the joiner that puts one event beside another — jôkhon
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: two chapters back, the joiner that puts one event beside another — *jôkhon*]

segments.text: ট (ṭô).
You have been carrying three corners of a square without being shown the square.

utterances: tongue on the teeth. voice off: ত tô. voice on: দ dô.
tongue curled back. voice off: ট ṭô. voice on: ড ḍô.

segments.text: Two switches, four letters. ট (ṭô) is the one the book never filled in: the tongue curled back to the ridge, exactly where you put it for ড, and the voice switched off, exactly as you do for ত. If you can make the other three you can already make this one — you have never been asked to.
An English t lands between the two rows, which is the same trap দ and ড set. To an English ear ত and ট (ṭô) are one letter. They are not, and they spell different words.
With the mātrā:
ট (ṭô) + া becomes টা (-ṭā).
Hold on to that syllable. It is the shape of the next four lessons, and it is the reason this letter could not wait any longer.

segments.instruction: ট (ṭô)
টা (-ṭā)
ত then ট (ṭô) — teeth, then curled back, voice off for both
segments.source: [YOU SAY: **ত** then **ট** — teeth, then curled back, voice off for both]

segments.instruction: ট (ṭô) then ড — curled back for both, voice off then on
segments.source: [YOU SAY: **ট** then **ড** — curled back for both, voice off then on]

segments.instruction: ত ট (ṭô) দ ড

segments.text: Which two switches make the square? (Where the tongue is, and whether the voice is on.) Which letter is ট (ṭô) with the voice switched on? (ড.) And which is it with the tongue brought forward onto the teeth? (ত.)
Source: Unicode Bengali chart.

lessons.title: টা (-ṭā) — the ending that means "the"
lessons.gloss: the classifier — the suffix that does the work English gives to the word "the", and that Bengali will not count a noun without

segments.text: Write the letter from the lesson before, then write it with the mātrā. Then say জামা.
জামা — jāmā — shirt.
জামাটা — jāmāṭā — the shirt.
চা — chā — tea.
চাটা — chāṭā — the tea.

Bengali has no word for the. Thirty chapters of this book have taught nouns that float free — shirt, tea, brother — with no way to say you mean that one, the one we are both thinking of. The way you say it is not a word in front. It is টা (-ṭā), stuck on the end.
Nothing goes between the noun and it, and nothing comes before the noun. The noun and its ending are written as one word.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: why this is called a classifier and not an article

segments.text: An article does one job: it says definite. টা (-ṭā) does that and one more. Bengali will not put a number directly on a noun, so টা (-ṭā) is also the piece a count has to pass through — you will meet that in the next lesson.
There is a polite twin, টি, used for people and in careful writing:
ভাইটা — bhāiṭā — the brother, plainly.
ভাইটি — bhāiṭi — the brother, respectfully.
Same slot, same job, different warmth. Learn টা (-ṭā) and recognise টি.

segments.instruction: jāmāṭā — the shirt
chāṭā — the tea
bhāiṭā, then the polite bhāiṭi
the red one — lāl jāmāṭā

segments.text: Where does টা (-ṭā) go — in front of the noun or on the end of it? (On the end, written as one word.) Does Bengali have a word for the? (No — this ending is what it has instead.) And which form would you use of a person you were being careful about? (টি.)
Source: Unicode Bengali chart.

lessons.title: একটা (ekṭā) — a, one
lessons.gloss: a, one — the numeral এক passing through the classifier, which is the only way Bengali lets a number touch a noun

segments.text: Say the shirt. Then read এক.
একটা জামা — ekṭā jāmā — a shirt.
একটা বন্ধু — ekṭā bôndhu — a friend.

Chapter twenty-four taught you to count এক দুই তিন চার পাঁচ, and then gave you nothing to count. This is why. এক cannot sit next to a noun. Bengali makes a number reach its noun through the classifier, and এক plus টা (-ṭā) is একটা (ekṭā) — which then means both one and a, because in Bengali those are the same thought.
So the ending you learned one lesson ago turns out to have been two doors:
জামাটা — the shirt, the one we mean.
একটা (ekṭā) জামা — a shirt, any one.
Same টা (-ṭā). Nothing in front of it, or a number in front of it.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: where the ending goes, and it moves

segments.text: Watch which word carries the suffix:

utterances: the shirt. Bengali: জামাটা. the ending is on: the noun.
a shirt. Bengali: একটা (ekṭā) জামা. the ending is on: the number.

segments.text: When a number turns up, the classifier leaves the noun and attaches to the number instead. That is one rule, and it is the rule that will carry every count you ever make in this language.

segments.instruction: ekṭā jāmā — a shirt
ekṭā bôndhu — a friend
the pair, back to back — jāmāṭā, then ekṭā jāmā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the pair, back to back — *jāmāṭā*, then *ekṭā jāmā*]

segments.instruction: a tea — ekṭā chā

segments.text: Can এক stand next to a noun on its own? (No — it goes through the classifier.) When a number appears, which word carries টা (-ṭā)? (The number, not the noun.) And what two English words does একটা (ekṭā) cover? (A, and one.)
Source: Unicode Bengali chart.

lessons.title: আরেকটা (ārekṭā) — another one
lessons.gloss: another one — আর plus এক plus the classifier, and the second half of the pair Bengali uses to hand out one thing at a time

segments.text: Say a shirt. Then say the joiner from chapter twenty-eight that means and.
আরেকটা চা — ārekṭā chā — another tea.
Take the word apart and it is already three things you own:
আর (and) + এক (one) + টা (-ṭā) (the classifier) becomes আরেকটা (ārekṭā).
Which is why it does not merely mean a different one. It means one more, with the and still inside it.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the pair that hands things out one at a time

segments.text: Bengali uses একটা … আরেকটা (ārekṭā) as a fixed pair to run down a list of things one by one, the way English uses one … another:
একটা লাল, আরেকটা কালো — ekṭā lāl, ārekṭā kālo — one red, another black.

This is the first time in this book that two things can be picked out and set side by side as separate items. Before the classifier existed there was no way to say one of anything, so there was no way to say another either.

segments.instruction: ārekṭā chā — another tea
the pair — ekṭā lāl, ārekṭā kālo
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the pair — *ekṭā lāl, ārekṭā kālo*]

segments.instruction: two shirts, one at a time — ekṭā jāmā, ārekṭā jāmā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: two shirts, one at a time — *ekṭā jāmā, ārekṭā jāmā*]

segments.instruction: the three pieces inside the word — ār, ek, ṭā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the three pieces inside the word — *ār*, *ek*, *ṭā*]

segments.text: What three pieces is আরেকটা (ārekṭā) built from? (আর, এক and টা (-ṭā).) What does the first piece add to the meaning? (And — so it is one more, rather than only a different one.) And what is the word it pairs with? (একটা.)
Source: Unicode Bengali chart.

blocks.title: Guided Practice: the distant band — every noun in the book, picked out one at a time

segments.text: This is what the chapter bought. Chapters ten to fifteen taught a pantry, a family, a face and a wardrobe, and not one of those nouns could be pointed at as the one or counted as a one. Every one of them can now. Take them cold, from memory.

segments.text: Does Bengali have a word for the? (No — it has this ending.) When a number stands in front, which word carries the ending? (The number.) Which form is the careful one, for people? (টি.) And which letter had to be taught before any of this chapter could be written down? (ট (ṭô).)
Source: Unicode Bengali chart.
